$comment: Asset publication policy. `role` is MEASURED from the production bundle and is re-derivable; `disposition` is a DECISION and is not. Do not overwrite dispositions from a re-scan.

policy.rationale: Uncertainty is sufficient grounds to exclude. We do not attempt to separate brand-private from licence-private until provenance is established, because the cost of being wrong is asymmetric: an over-cautious exclusion costs a replacement asset, an over-confident publication cannot be undone.
policy.private_assets_live_in: ThomasCaruso/rot-royale-content, under assets/ — the SAME private repository as the gameplay corpus. One repo, one token, one CONTENT_COMMIT.
policy.retrieved_as: a BUILD dependency, never a runtime one. The backend already fetches this repo into its artifact because the server reads the corpus while serving; the frontend build fetches the assets/ subtree of the same repo at the same pin, because the bundle consumes art while building. Both are build-time; neither reaches for the network at runtime.
policy.why_not_a_separate_assets_repo: Considered and rejected. The case for splitting was release cadence — art changes would otherwise mint a new CONTENT_COMMIT and redeploy the backend to ship a recoloured button. That is real but minor, and it was outweighed: every retrieval path is new surface area, and the FIRST one produced two defects that only appeared on real infrastructure (a production-mode import deadlock and a cross-device rename). A second repo would add a second token, a second pin and a second set of failure modes while buying nothing — the frontend has to fetch its art either way. One revision number describing all private material is also easier to reason about than two that can disagree. Accepted cost: a theme tweak redeploys the backend. Minutes, no downtime.

assets.note: Committed deliberately: a crawler never runs a Google Fonts @import and Pillow's builtin face is illegible at headline sizes. Both licences permit redistribution. Do not rename the TTFs — the NOTICE refers to them by filename.
